text.title: From Overhead Ratio to Verdict
text.summary: Routing from the two measured numbers to one of three verdicts: leave alone, compress, restructure. Most systems that reach here route to compress, which needs no new machinery.

decision-tree.root-question: What is the measured overhead_ratio — tokens spent on index and candidates per token of delivered body — and where does median_tokens_per_lookup sit against the published reference band?

conclusion.verdict: STOP. There is no ledger yet. Instrument the full lookup — routing, index, candidates, body — collect ten real queries, and return. Do not let an estimate enter this tree; downstream methodologies cannot distinguish it from a measurement.

LEAVE ALONE. Retrieval is near the published flat-vector band (879-954 query tokens, GraphRAG-Bench 2025-06-06). Spend the effort on answer quality, not structure. Record the ledger as a baseline and move on.

COMPRESS THE INDEX. The bill is the routing tier, not the content. Shard any index above a declared read ceiling, replace restated summaries with short discriminators, and re-measure. This is the cheapest fix and needs no new retrieval machinery.

COMPRESS THE CANDIDATE SET. Candidates dominate on a mostly single-hop query mix: tighten k, add reranking, and re-measure. Flat retrieval with reranking beat graph retrieval on both fact corpora at roughly 1/40th the query tokens.

branch.when: overhead_ratio >= 5.0 AND multi_hop_share >= 0.3 AND compression_already_applied == true

conclusion.verdict: RESTRUCTURE — and only now. Hand median_tokens_per_lookup to `context-graph-engineering` as cost_incumbent_tokens. Any candidate structure must be measured on this same query set, model and tokenizer, with its build cost amortised against corpus change frequency.

OVERLAY, whichever branch above applied: more than half the lookups fail. This is a quality defect wearing a cost costume — route to retrieval evaluation first, because cheapening a retriever that already misses makes the cost-per-correct-answer worse, not better.
